req.title: /status/<code> accepts POST
req.statement: The system shall accept POST requests on /status/<code> and return the requested code.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /status/<code> must return the requested HTTP status code. I design tests covering: (1) a standard 2xx positive case (200), (2) a negative/client-error case (400), (3) boundary cases at the edges of common status code ranges (100, 299, 300, 500), (4) an invalid code negative path, and (5) a 5xx server-error code. Each test uses exact status code assertions to catch comparison-operator and constant mutations. Tests also verify that the route accepts POST specifically (not just any method), and that boundary codes ±1 are handled correctly.

tests.name: test_post_status_200_positive
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_status_200_positive():
    r = client.post('/status/200')
    assert r.status_code == 200

test_post_status_200_positive()

tests.name: test_post_not_get_method_accepted
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: GET /status/200 and verify 200 returned (to confirm POST is distinct)
expected: GET /status/200 also returns exactly 200 (route supports both)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-046: DT — POST method specifically accepted on /status/<code>
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_not_get_method_accepted():
    r_post = client.post('/status/200')
    assert r_post.status_code == 200
    r_get = client.get('/status/200')
    assert r_get.status_code == 200

test_post_not_get_method_accepted()
